controllingSource: Adopted 2026–2027 OER Part B, Art. B4.1–B4.2 and Appendix 1 printed pp. 15–19; transition in Appendix 2 p. 20.
reconciliation: The common core is 60 first-year, 42 later basic, 6 philosophy and 12 thesis EC. Add 30 Psychology and 30 free elective EC. The dated catalogue omitted Philosophy from the Psychology tree although the current course is offered in block 1. The regulations require it for this route. Cognitive Modelling is a single common 6 EC course with flexible placement. The schedule uses the year-two placement per the Appendix footnote and the block-four offering.

The OER explicitly sets CLC eligibility for restricted electives at 60 CLC EC, with the dedicated 6 EC Brain & Cognition course additionally required for B&C electives. The older Psychology route describes the same exceptions. Generic Psychology entry text applies to regular Psychology students and directs others to separate rules. Select the three B&C courses and one Current Topics option. Year two takes Perception in block 4 and Memory in block 5. Year three takes the remaining Neuroscience course in block 4 and Consciousness in block 1.

The OER permits 30 free EC across years two and three, overriding the catalogue tree’s sample split of 6 and 24. The example uses all 30 in year three. By the start of the thesis, the student can complete 138 named pre-thesis EC, including the CLC core and specialisation, even before free electives. Advanced Statistics is offered before the project in block 4. The thesis counts once at 12 EC in blocks 5 and 6.
